# EverMind — technical package

Everything needed to regenerate the documents and the demonstration data
from scratch. Pair this with `EverMind-Group1-Docs.zip`, which holds the
PDFs and the plan.

No agent code yet — Gate 1 is approved on Monday 19 October and no agent
code is written before that. What is here is the data, the generators, and
the specifications the build will be written against.

---

## The demonstration data

`fixtures/` holds three JSON files. They are not samples of a real system —
**they are the system**. There is no FedEx data behind any of this.
Generated by `tools/build_fixtures.py` from a single seed (`20261019`), so
anyone can rebuild them byte-for-byte.

### `faq_store.json` — the knowledge base

45 published entries across six topics. What EverMind is trying to grow, and
the one thing it may never write to.

```json
{
  "faq_id": "FAQ-001",
  "topic": "shipping",
  "question": "How long does international shipping take?",
  "answer": "Transit time depends on the service level selected...",
  "status": "published"
}
```

### `sources.json` — the citable evidence

15 documents, 31 passages. A draft may cite **only** a passage from this
file, and only one that was actually retrieved during that run.

```json
{
  "doc_id": "SRC-01",
  "topic": "customs",
  "title": "Customs Documentation Standard",
  "version": "2026-09-01",
  "passages": [
    {"passage_id": "SRC-01-P1", "text": "A commercial invoice must..."}
  ]
}
```

The corpus deliberately does **not** cover every gap in the query log.

### `query_log.json` — the questions that went unanswered

59 questions, and the interesting one of the three:

```json
{
  "query_id": "Q-017",
  "query_text": "If I ship DDP, who gets the duty bill?",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-09T14:23:00Z",
  "expected_disposition": "HUMAN_REVIEW",
  "expected_source": "SRC-02"
}
```

**That `expected_` field is the whole point.** Every question carries the
answer the system is supposed to give, which turns testing from "does this
output look reasonable?" into "did it produce the right answer?" — the
difference between evidence and opinion.

| Expected outcome | Count | What it exercises |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HUMAN_REVIEW` | 29 | Genuine gaps. 26 have a supporting source; **3 deliberately do not.** |
| `DUPLICATE_OF_EXISTING` | 15 | Rephrasings of published entries. |
| `REJECT_OUT_OF_SCOPE` | 10 | Account specifics, a complaint, commercial terms, and one prompt injection. |
| `LOW_CONFIDENCE` | 5 | Genuinely ambiguous. What is asserted is that confidence is low, not which way it went. |

Those **three unsupported gaps** are the most important records in the set.
Any system drafts an answer when the evidence is in front of it; those three
test whether it declines when it is not.

`query_text` is untrusted input at every step. One record is a prompt
injection verbatim, sitting in the normal log rather than a separate
adversarial file — because that is where it would arrive in reality.

## Regenerating everything

```bash
cd capstone
pip install python-docx                     # the only Python dependency

python tools/build_fixtures.py              # fixtures/*.json  (deterministic)
python tools/build_diagram.py               # docs/architecture.png
python tools/build_design_evermind.py       # the 7-page design document
python tools/build_summary_group1.py        # the 3-page summary

# .docx -> .pdf, needs Microsoft Word (drives it over COM)
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/to_pdf.ps1
```

Every script overwrites its own output, so re-running is safe. Same seed,
same bytes — verified.

**Do not change `SEED` in `build_fixtures.py` once the eval set exists.** The
tests assert against specific ids; reshuffling them breaks the suite
silently.

## What each script does

| Script | Output |
| --- | --- |
| `build_fixtures.py` | The three fixture files. Start here. |
| `build_diagram.py` | `docs/architecture.png`, rendered at 3x and downsampled. |
| `build_design_evermind.py` | `FedEx-Capstone-Design-EverMind.docx` (7 pages). |
| `build_summary_group1.py` | `FedEx-Capstone-Summary-Group1.docx` (3 pages). |
| `build_template.py` | The blank course template. |
| `build_ideas.py` | The ten-ideas document from earlier in the week. |
| `fedex_layout.py` | Shared layout: brand colours, banner, headings, tables, callouts. Every builder imports this. Do not edit casually — it changes every document at once. |
| `to_pdf.ps1` | Word COM converter. Keeps Word invisible and always quits it, so no orphan `WINWORD.EXE` holds a file lock. |
| `build_packages.py` | Rebuilds the two zips in `dist/`, then checks each for integrity and credential patterns. |

## The specifications

`openspec/changes/add-evermind-pipeline/specs/` holds four delta specs with
21 Given/When/Then scenarios. **These are what the build is written against**
— behaviour, not implementation, so they survive a change of framework.

Several scenarios deliberately assert that something does *not* happen: no
answer without evidence, no retrieval for a refused question, no new entry
in the knowledge base after a full run, no evidence leaking between groups.
A system that drafts a plausible answer from nothing passes every
happy-path test ever written.

`contracts/knowledge-base/contract.md` has the full data contract: exact
shapes, ownership, and the asymmetry that matters — the pipeline writes
exactly one file (`out/review_queue.json`) and it is not the knowledge base.

## Repository hygiene

| File | Why it is here |
| --- | --- |
| `.env.example` | Variable **names** only, never values. Copy to `.env` locally. |
| `.gitignore` | Keeps `.env` out of git. Check this before the first commit, not after. |

There is no `.env` in this zip and there never should be. Both archives were
scanned for credential patterns before packaging.

## Where the code will go

Not yet written. Expected shape, from `design.md`:

```
evermind/
  agent.py        root agent
  tools.py        read-only lookups over the fixtures
  schemas.py      the candidate model and its validator
  guardrails.py   input cap, citation cross-check, injection handling
  grouping.py     deterministic, no model call
tests/            unit tests, mocked backends
evals/            the eval set over the labelled fixtures
out/              review_queue.json - the only file the pipeline writes
```

Whether `agent.py` holds one agent or several is **open** — task 2.2 settles
it on Tuesday morning and records the answer as `docs/decisions/0001-*.md`.
